newsitem.title: INDIA: Japan's Marubeni in Indian iron ore deal.
newsitem.headline: Japan's Marubeni in Indian iron ore deal.

text.p: Japanese trading company Marubeni Corp signed a $110 million joint venture pact with an Indian partner on Monday to construct a large offshore dock for the export of iron ores from India.

Marubeni and Sociedade de Fomento Industrial Ltd said in a statement in the Indian capital that the 50/50 joint venture would build a berth, or dock, 10 km (six miles) off the coast of the western Indian state of Goa for the export of iron ores.

The tie-up, called FOMAR Ltd, would develop new iron ore mines in the southern Indian state of Karnataka expected to produce about 1.5 million tonnes of iron ore each year. The total project cost is about $110 million, it said.

"We are very pleased with the joint venture and hope this will help India earn foreign currency," Marubeni director F. Ishi told reporters in New Delhi. The Japanese executive said the venture would sell iron ore to Japan, Indonesia and Malaysia, as well as to the Middle East.
The offshore stockyard and berth would be made of concrete caissons measuring 200 metres (220 yards) in length and 45 metres (50 yards) in width, the statement said.
The dock will be able to accommodate vessels of up to 200,000 dead weight tonnage (DWT), it said. About 450,000 tonnes of bulk materials will be able to be stocked there, it said.
The statement said it would be the first time that concrete caissons had been used for iron ore loading facilities.
The offshore berth will also be used for imports of coal for steel and power plants. The firms expect the dock to be able to handle about four million tonnes of iron ore and coal each year.
Sociedade de Fomento Chairman Auduth Timblo said the offshore stockyard "will facilitate docking of large sea vessels and lead to economies of scale in transporting iron ore and coal".
A detailed feasibility study will be finished by May 1997 and construction will start in June 1997, with a target for commissioning of October 1999, the statement said.
